method: Qualitative inspection by the coding assistant of all 96 responses, not blinded. The shortlist is exploratory and requires rolling validation.
findings: All 96 responses are complete. Neither the technical-memory obsession nor genre labeling reappeared in these four scenes with the new prompt.
Higher temperature sometimes chooses a better detail, but does not consistently improve the observation. Errors about objects and actors occur at low and high temperatures.
The short prose and detailed cards use identical factual sentences and ordering; formatting alone has no decisive qualitative advantage in this small screen.
The compact cards retain enough background for these scenes, but later parts of the game may require facts omitted by this compression.
Most comments remain entirely about the scene. Explicit references to Briggs are not used as a success criterion.

examples_to_audit.assessment: Good specific observation: the instruction to get comfortable makes imprisonment sound routine.
Useful association between the failed clasp and the precarious protection being offered; a reading of the scene, not a production cause.
Contradicts the source by calling the barrels' contents seemingly identical; the game identifies rum and water.
Invents the bottle as a means of delivering a message to Lafond.
Conflates the bottle taken by the protagonist with Crulley's plan for mischief.
Also associates the seized bottle with Crulley's plans without support; this candidate is not uniformly reliable.
Adds money to the coffer's allotment; the displayed history does not establish money.
Evocative but uses Markdown italics despite the plain-text instruction.

finalists.reason: Current runtime baseline, needed to judge the effect of both changes.
Detailed factual reference with moderate variation; promising associations but some actor confusion to check.
Compact low-temperature candidate with several good observations; checks whether temperature increase is necessary.
Compact high-temperature candidate with expressive examples; checks long-run factual and formatting reliability.
